title: code-review-graph backend: process/prereq/CLI specs + capture live fixtures
description: Flesh out CodeReviewGraphBackend's non-adapter surface and capture ground-truth fixtures. Implement its ProcessSpec (binary 'code-review-graph', serveArgs ['serve']), PrereqSpec (versionArgs ['--version'], a compatible-version predicate, installHint 'pip install code-review-graph'), and CliMap (init->build, sync->update, status->detect-changes/status with output parsers). Then PROBE the locally-installed `code-review-graph serve` to capture the REAL MCP tool output JSON for every tool the adapters will need, and commit those as fixtures under tests/graph/fixtures/cr-graph/. Use `git show 6ed3f77~1:src/graph/client.ts` (agent-bober's original code-review-graph adapter) as a shape reference. No response adapters yet — those consume these fixtures in Sprints 5-6.

successCriteria.description: Build + typecheck pass with zero errors.

CodeReviewGraphBackend.processSpec = {binary:'code-review-graph' (overridable via config.graph.codeReviewGraphPath), serveArgs:['serve']}; prereqSpec.installHint = 'pip install code-review-graph'; the generalized prereq detects a real `code-review-graph --version` (skipIf-gated integration test) and, with execa mocked, a valid version passes and a clearly-incompatible one fails with the pip install hint.

CliMap maps init->['build'], sync->['update', ...paths] (or the documented incremental verb), status->the detect-changes/status verb, each with an output parser. parseSync/parseStatus are unit-tested against captured CLI output samples.

Real MCP tool output JSON is captured from a live `code-review-graph serve` (via the initialize + tools/call probe) for every tool the adapters need — at minimum semantic_search_nodes_tool, get_impact_radius_tool, get_review_context_tool, get_architecture_overview_tool, detect_changes_tool, query_graph_tool, traverse_graph_tool — and committed as tests/graph/fixtures/cr-graph/<tool>.json. Each fixture is the exact unwrapped payload (result.content[].text parsed) the transport would hand an adapter.

resolveGraphBackend selects the code-review-graph backend when config.graph.backend='code-review-graph' and, in an integration context, when only cr-graph is installed. A skipIf-gated integration test starts a real `code-review-graph serve` and completes the MCP initialize handshake through the (Sprint-2 parameterized) transport.

If the live cr-graph binary cannot be located during this sprint, the sprint DOES NOT invent shapes: it records the blocker in the sprint notes, seeds fixtures from the git-history reference (6ed3f77~1) marked as provisional, and leaves a documented follow-up to refresh them from a live run. (This criterion is satisfied by either a real capture OR an explicit, documented provisional-fixture fallback — never by silently guessed JSON.)
Full suite green (no NEW failures); tokensave path unaffected; lint clean.

nonGoals: Do NOT implement the response adapters (search/impact/etc. narrowing) — Sprints 5-6 consume these fixtures.
Do NOT add a live cr-graph test to the DEFAULT CI path — cr-graph integration tests must be skipIf-gated on the binary being present.
Do NOT modify the tokensave backend or the shared transport wire protocol.
Do NOT install code-review-graph for the user or add it as an npm/pip dependency of this project.
stopConditions: CodeReviewGraphBackend has real process/prereq/cli specs, real (or explicitly-provisional) fixtures are committed for every needed tool, detection selects it, and the transport can initialize-handshake a real cr-graph serve; suite + lint green
definitionOfDone: CodeReviewGraphBackend describes its process/prereq/cli; committed fixtures under tests/graph/fixtures/cr-graph/ capture the real MCP output for every adapter tool (or documented-provisional from git history if the binary was unreachable, with a follow-up); detection + a skipIf live handshake work; tokensave path untouched; suite + lint green.
assumptions: code-review-graph is a Python 3.10+ package exposing `code-review-graph serve` (MCP) and CLI verbs build/update/watch/serve/detect-changes/daemon (per its README). Its ~30 MCP tools include semantic_search_nodes_tool, get_impact_radius_tool, get_review_context_tool, query_graph_tool, detect_changes_tool, traverse_graph_tool, get_architecture_overview_tool, build_or_update_graph_tool. Store dir is .code-review-graph/.

The binary was NOT on this shell's PATH at plan time (likely a venv/pipx install). The generator must LOCATE it: try `command -v code-review-graph`, `python -m code_review_graph --version`, common venv paths, or ask via config.graph.codeReviewGraphPath. If truly unreachable, invoke the sc-4-6 provisional-fixture fallback.

Probe technique (same pattern as the tokensave probe in the 6-1-compat sprint): pipe an initialize request, a notifications/initialized, then a tools/call for each tool into `code-review-graph serve` and capture stdout; unwrap result.content[].text and JSON.parse it. Save each parsed payload as a fixture. Tools/call arguments for cr-graph may differ from tokensave (e.g. a query string, a file path, a node id) — capture the argument shape too.

git history reference: `git show 6ed3f77~1:src/graph/client.ts` shows the ORIGINAL adapter with TOOL {search:'semantic_search_nodes', query:'query_graph', impact:'get_impact_radius', reviewContext:'get_review_context', overview:'get_architecture_overview', changes:'detect_changes'} and the row types it expected — a strong prior for shapes, though names now carry a `_tool` suffix and JSON may have evolved.

PrereqSpec compatibility for cr-graph: without a documented supported range, accept any parseable version for now and record the tested version; tightening the range is a follow-up. installHint is 'pip install code-review-graph'.
config.graph.codeReviewGraphPath (added in Sprint 3, optional) overrides the binary name, mirroring tokensavePath.
generatorNotes:
Read FIRST: the Sprint-3 CodeReviewGraphBackend stub + registry, the Sprint-2 process/prereq/cli specs on the tokensave backend (as the template), src/graph/mcp-client.ts (probe technique), and `git show 6ed3f77~1:src/graph/client.ts` (original cr-graph shapes).

STEP 1 — LOCATE the binary: `command -v code-review-graph` || check config.graph.codeReviewGraphPath || try a venv/pipx path || `python -m code_review_graph --version`. Record the resolved path. If unreachable, go to STEP 4b.

STEP 2 — implement CodeReviewGraphBackend process/prereq/cli specs by analogy to tokensave-backend: processSpec {binary, serveArgs:['serve']}, prereqSpec {versionArgs:['--version'], isCompatible, installHint:'pip install code-review-graph'}, cliMap {initArgs:['build'], syncArgs:(p)=>['update',...p], statusArgs, parseSync, parseStatus}. Capture a couple of real `code-review-graph build`/`update` output samples to write parseSync against.

STEP 3 — CAPTURE MCP fixtures: for each needed tool, run the initialize+tools/call probe against the located `code-review-graph serve` (on THIS repo so nodes exist), unwrap result.content[].text, JSON.parse, and write tests/graph/fixtures/cr-graph/<tool>.json (the parsed payload). Also note each tool's argument shape in a small README or a fixtures/cr-graph/_args.json. Cover: semantic_search_nodes_tool, get_impact_radius_tool, get_review_context_tool, get_architecture_overview_tool, detect_changes_tool, query_graph_tool, traverse_graph_tool.

STEP 4 — tests: unit-test the prereq (execa mocked) + parseSync/parseStatus against captured CLI samples; add a skipIf(!crGraphAvailable) integration test that initialize-handshakes a real serve. STEP 4b (fallback only): if the binary was unreachable, seed fixtures from the git-history shapes, mark them `// PROVISIONAL — refresh from live run` and add the follow-up note; keep the skipIf test so a later live run validates.

Run `npm run build && npm run typecheck && npx vitest run tests/graph/` + full suite + lint. Commit `bober(sprint-4): code-review-graph process/prereq/cli specs + captured MCP fixtures`.
evaluatorNotes: The integrity bar here is NO INVENTED SHAPES. sc-4-4: open the committed tests/graph/fixtures/cr-graph/*.json — they must be plausible real cr-graph outputs (not hand-written stubs mirroring tokensave's shape). If the generator claims a live capture, spot-check that the fixtures differ structurally from tokensave's Ts*Row shapes (cr-graph is a different engine) and match the original 6ed3f77~1 field names where applicable. sc-4-6: if the generator took the provisional fallback, CONFIRM the fixtures are explicitly marked provisional AND a follow-up is recorded — do not accept silently-guessed JSON presented as real. sc-4-2/4-3: mock execa; pip install hint present; parseSync handles the captured cr-graph 'build'/'update' output. sc-4-5: if cr-graph is installed, the skipIf integration test must complete the handshake; if absent it must skip (not fail). sc-4-7: tokensave path + full suite unaffected. Reject if fixtures look like tokensave outputs with renamed keys, or if the cr-graph binary was reachable but the generator skipped live capture.
